subject: Clarify deployment boundary options and data custody for HealthSync
messages:
From: Lily Zhang <lily.zhang@healthsync.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood deployment options & data isolation

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the quick walkthrough. A few notes from our side after the call so we can triage next steps with our security team: 

- Data classification: majority PHI (clinical notes + IDs). We need to ensure no customer data is available to other tenants and that any persistent storage is under our control or certified to our standards.
- Key management: healthsync requires customer-managed KMS/HSM or an equivalent path where keys are not accessible by vendor staff.
- Auditability: immutable logs required for 7 years, with the ability to export to our SIEM.
- Network: all inference traffic must stay within our VPC or on-prem network; egress to shared endpoints is a blocker.

Given that, we're trying to understand the practical difference between Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem). Can that be summarized specifically around custody (who holds keys), network boundary (VPC peering vs managed endpoints), and a quick list of controls you can provide as evidence (SOC2 date, pen test report, enclave/HSM support)?.

I'm attaching our internal data-classification doc so you can align answers to specific fields. Also looping in our legal (cc) — they may want to see how audit retention and KMS integration map to contract terms.

Can we do a 30-minute technical sync tomorrow with your infra lead (Ben) and our infra/security engineer? Prefer morning PST.

Thanks,
Lily
Lily Zhang
Head of Platform Engineering, HealthSync
----

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood deployment options & data isolation

Hi Lily — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Recap below + a proposed next-step plan.

Recap / quick answers (high level):
- Custody / keys:
  - Dedicated: control plane remains hosted by Redwood; we support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) for at-rest encryption keys used for model artifacts and cached outputs. Keys are in the customer-managed KMS and Redwood never stores plaintext keys.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): full option for customer-hosted control plane or VPC peering with customer-managed NAT; for on-prem, keys and credential material can remain entirely on your side.
- Network boundary:
  - Dedicated: traffic terminates on dedicated GPU pools with strict tenant isolation; however control plane APIs are hosted by Redwood and require egress to our endpoints (TLS). We can lock down egress and provide IP allowlists + VPC peering in many regions.
  - Private: traffic remains inside your VPC or on-prem and does not egress to Redwood endpoints (if you choose the private control plane).
- Auditability: both models support exportable audit logs. For Dedicated we store audit logs in a customer-dedicated bucket (optional) and can configure S3 export hooks; Private gives you full ownership of logs in your environment.

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-minute technical sync tomorrow at 10:00 AM PST (Ben + our infra lead) to walk your infra/security lead through network/topology and KMS specifics.
2) I'll attach a short one-pager that contrasts Dedicated vs Private from an isolation/custody perspective (see attached).
3) If that looks good, we'll provide a checklist mapping controls to artifacts (SOC2 scope, recent pen test, KMS/HSM integration notes).

Question for your infra/security engineer: do you need WORM-style immutable storage for logs enforced by the storage layer, or would signed/hashed export bundles be sufficient?

Thanks — Ben will join the call for the technical deep dive.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
redwood.com
----
Attachment: redwood-dedicated-private-one-pager.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

Hi Lily — Ben here (infra at Redwood). Quick technical clarifications to prep for tomorrow's sync: 

- KV/cache persistence: by default, inference KV cache is ephemeral per-request and stored in GPU memory; we can configure persistent cache to a customer-dedicated encrypted store for low-latency reuse, and those stores can be customer-owned buckets in Dedicated.
- Keys & HSM: we support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. For customers requiring FIPS 140-2 HSM-backed keys, we have an HSM integration path (customer provides key material or we integrate with partner HSM in the region).
- Network topology options:
  - Dedicated + VPC peering: control plane remains hosted, inference traffic flows over peered links to dedicated GPU pools; we can offer strict IP allowlisting and private link in supported clouds.
  - Private (VPC on-prem): full data path stays inside your network; management plane can be staged so that only operational telemetry (optional) reaches Redwood.
- Logs & retention: for the 7-year requirement, we recommend exported immutable storage on your side (S3 + Object Lock/WORM). If you need vendor-side retention, we can discuss contractual SLA and retention buckets but that requires a separate compliance attachment.

I can walk through a reference topology diagram and a minimal checklist for HSM/KMS integration on the call.

Ben
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel and Ben — that helps a lot.

Quick replies and scope alignment: 
- For keys: HealthSync prefers keys in our KMS (Cloud HSM). If Redwood can integrate with our HSM and never hold plaintext keys, that satisfies our requirement.
- Network: VPC peering or private link for Dedicated would work as long as you can guarantee no traffic is routed over public internet and we have IP allowlist control.
- Logs: we prefer export to our S3 with Object Lock/WORM; please include an example export workflow in the checklist.

We're available for the 10:00 AM PST slot — please send calendar invite. I'll have our infra/security engineer and one counsel rep on the call to validate the checklist items. I'm attaching a short infra-question spreadsheet — it lists the contract-level asks our legal team will want to map to product controls.

Appreciate the speedy responses.

Lily
